metadata.title: A Simple Proof of the Johnson--Lindenstrauss Extension Theorem

nodes.name: Lipschitz constant
nodes.statement: For a mapping $f:T\to Y$ between metric spaces, $\Lip(f)=\sup_{x\ne y \in T} d_Y(f(x),f(y))/d_T(x,y)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Smallest constant such that $f$ is Lipschitz.

nodes.name: Johnson--Lindenstrauss Extension Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be an arbitrary $n$-point metric space, $X\supset T$ a superspace, $\mathcal H$ a Hilbert space, and $f:T\to \mathcal H$. Then there exists $F:X\to \mathcal H$ with $F|_T=f$ and $\Lip(F) \lesssim \sqrt{\log n} \cdot \Lip(f)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Any Lipschitz map from an $n$-point subset into a Hilbert space extends to the whole superspace with Lipschitz constant blown up by $O(\sqrt{\log n})$.

nodes.name: McShane Extension Theorem
nodes.statement: For any real-valued Lipschitz map $u_\omega:T\to \R$, there exists an extension $U_\omega:X\to \R$ with $U_\omega|_T=u_\omega$ and $\Lip(U_\omega)=\Lip(u_\omega)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Real-valued Lipschitz maps on subsets extend to the whole space without increasing the Lipschitz constant.
assumptions: $T \subset X$ a subset of a metric space
nodes.origin_citation: McShane; also Weaver, Lipschitz Algebras, Theorem 1.33

nodes.name: Maximum of squared Gaussians bound
nodes.statement: For $m\ge 2$ standard Gaussians $G_1,\ldots,G_m$ with any dependence structure, $\E[\max\{G_1^2,\ldots,G_m^2\}] \lesssim \log m$.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected maximum of $m$ squared standard Gaussians (any dependence) is $O(\log m)$.
assumptions: $G_1,\ldots,G_m$ are standard Gaussian random variables (with arbitrary joint dependence)

nodes.name: Gaussian linear isometry into $L_2(\Omega)$
nodes.statement: If $g_1,\ldots,g_n$ are i.i.d. standard Gaussians, then $\sum_i x_i g_i$ is centered Gaussian with variance $\sum_i x_i^2$, hence $\|\sum_i x_i g_i\|_{L_2(\Omega)} = \|(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\|_2$.
nodes.statement_clean: The map $k(x)=\sum_i x_i g_i$ is an isometric isomorphism from $\R^n$ onto $k(\R^n)\subset L_2(\Omega)$.
assumptions: $g_1,\ldots,g_n$ are i.i.d. standard Gaussian random variables on $\Omega$
conclusions: $k:\R^n\to L_2(\Omega)$ defined by $k(x)=\sum_i x_i g_i$ is an isometry

nodes.name: Lipschitz bound on extension $U$
nodes.statement: $\| U(x)-U(y)\|_{L_2(\Omega)} \le d(x,y)\bigl( \E_\Omega \max_{s\ne t\in T} G_{f(s)-f(t)}^2 \bigr)^{1/2}$, where $G_z := \sum_i \frac{z_i}{\|z\|_2} g_i$.

nodes.name: Expected max of squared Gaussians is $\lesssim \log m$
nodes.statement: $\E[\max\{G_1^2,\ldots,G_m^2\}] \lesssim \log m$.

nodes.name: Proof of Johnson--Lindenstrauss Extension Theorem
nodes.statement: Embed $\R^n$ isometrically into $L_2(\Omega)$ via Gaussian coordinates, apply McShane extension to each coordinate, then project back to $\R^n$ and bound the resulting Lipschitz constant by the expected max of squared Gaussians.

nodes.name: Reduce to $\mathcal H = \R^n$ and $\Lip(f)=1$
nodes.statement: WLOG assume $\mathcal H=\R^n$ (so $f:T\to \R^n$) and rescale so that $\Lip(f)=1$.

nodes.name: Construct Gaussian isometry $k:\R^n \to L_2(\Omega)$
nodes.statement: Let $g_1,\ldots,g_n$ be i.i.d. standard Gaussians on $\Omega$, set $H=L_2(\Omega)$, and define $k(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_i x_i g_i$; then $k$ is an isometric isomorphism onto $k(\R^n)\subset H$.

nodes.name: Form $u=k\circ f$, write coordinatewise as $(u_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$
nodes.statement: Define $u:=k\circ f:T\to k(\R^n)$, which is $1$-Lipschitz; write $u=(u_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$.

nodes.name: Apply McShane extension coordinatewise
nodes.statement: For each $\omega\in\Omega$, extend $u_\omega:T\to \R$ to $U_\omega:X\to \R$ with $\Lip(U_\omega)=\Lip(u_\omega)$ by McShane; assemble $U:=(U_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}:X\to H$.

nodes.name: Project back to $\R^n$ via $F=k^{-1}\circ P\circ U$
nodes.statement: Using the orthogonal projection $P:H\to k(\R^n)$, set $F:=k^{-1}\circ P\circ U:X\to \R^n$, an extension of $f$ with $\Lip(F)\le \Lip(U)$ since $\Lip(k^{-1})=\Lip(P)=1$.

nodes.name: Bound $\Lip(U)$ by expected max of squared Gaussians
nodes.statement: Compute $\|U(x)-U(y)\|_{L_2(\Omega)}\le d(x,y)\bigl(\E_\Omega \max_{s\ne t\in T} G_{f(s)-f(t)}^2\bigr)^{1/2}$, where $G_z:=\sum_i \frac{z_i}{\|z\|_2} g_i$ are standard Gaussians.

nodes.name: Conclude using the $\log n$ bound on max of $n^2$ squared Gaussians
nodes.statement: Since $|T|=n$, the maximum is over at most $n^2$ squared Gaussians; by the bound $\E[\max\{G_1^2,\ldots,G_m^2\}]\lesssim \log m$, the right-hand side is $\lesssim d(x,y)\sqrt{\log n}$.

nodes.name: Proof of $\E[\max G_i^2] \lesssim \log m$
nodes.statement: Use the Gaussian tail bound $\Pr[G_i\ge t]\le e^{-t^2/2}$, the union bound, and integrate the tail; substituting $s=2\log m$ yields the conclusion.

nodes.name: Tail bound for individual squared Gaussian
nodes.statement: By the classical Gaussian tail bound $\Pr[G_i\ge t]\le e^{-t^2/2}$, hence $\Pr[G_i^2\ge t]\le 2e^{-t/2}$.

nodes.name: Union bound for the maximum
nodes.statement: Apply the union bound: $\Pr[\max\{G_1^2,\ldots,G_m^2\}\ge t]\le 2m e^{-t/2}$.

nodes.name: Integrate the tail and split at $s$
nodes.statement: For any $s\ge 0$, $\E[\max\{G_1^2,\ldots,G_m^2\}] \le s + \int_s^\infty 2m e^{-t/2}\,dt = s + 4m e^{-s/2}$.

nodes.name: Substitute $s=2\log m$
nodes.statement: Setting $s=2\log m$ (with $m\ge 2$) gives $\E[\max\{G_1^2,\ldots,G_m^2\}]\le 2\log m + 4 \lesssim \log m$.

nodes.name: Proof of McShane extension for finite domains
nodes.statement: Define $Q(x)=\min_{t\in T} q(t)+L d_X(x,t)$ for $L$-Lipschitz $q:T\to \R$ on a finite $T\subset X$; show $Q|_T=q$ and verify $L$-Lipschitzness via the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Define candidate extension $Q(x)=\min_{t\in T} q(t)+L d_X(x,t)$
nodes.statement: Let $T\subset X$ be finite and $q:T\to \R$ be $L$-Lipschitz; set $Q(x):=\min_{t\in T} q(t)+L d_X(x,t)$.

nodes.name: Verify $Q|_T = q$
nodes.statement: Using the Lipschitz condition on $q$, check that $Q(s)=q(s)$ for all $s\in T$.

nodes.name: Lipschitz bound for $Q$ via triangle inequality
nodes.statement: For $x,y\in X$, pick $t\in T$ with $Q(x)=q(t)+Ld_X(x,t)$; then $Q(y)\le q(t)+L d_X(y,t)\le q(t)+L d_X(x,t)+L d_X(x,y)=Q(x)+L d_X(x,y)$. By symmetry $|Q(x)-Q(y)|\le L d_X(x,y)$.

nodes.name: Alternative derivation via Ball's extension theorem
nodes.statement: As pointed out in Mendel--Naor 2006, Theorem~\ref{thm:JL} also follows from Ball's extension theorem combined with the Markov type 2 estimates of Naor--Peres--Schramm--Sheffield 2006.

nodes.name: Original proof relied on dimension reduction
nodes.statement: The original proof of the JL extension theorem in Johnson--Lindenstrauss 1984 introduced the celebrated JL lemma on dimension reduction; this note avoids both dimension reduction and the Kirszbraun extension theorem.
